name: OlympicArena
intro: OlympicArena 是覆盖七个科学领域与62项竞赛的双语多模态奥赛推理基准。论文定义11,163题及答案级、过程级协议；固定 Hugging Face 快照仅公开638题验证集与9,977题测试集，另有548题 OlympicArena-ot 未包含在该快照中。
org: Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, Soochow University, GAIR
build_method: 公开竞赛 PDF 与计算机题测试用例, Mathpix 转换与约30名理工科学生标注, 七项规则检查和异人复核, 竞赛内嵌入去重, GPT-4V 标签经人工核验
metric: 论文：准确率、计算机题 n=5 的无偏 Pass@1、过程步骤均分；公开代码：无方框时保留整段回答，计算机题有效 n 为成功提取的代码段数，并仅汇报验证集统计
modality: 文本, 图像, 多模态
task_type: 数学问题, 多学科推理
eval_feature: 双语, 多学科, 答案级与过程级评测, 认知与视觉推理标签
scale: 论文11,163题（548 OT + 638验证 + 9,977测试）；固定HF快照10,615题，不含548题OT；62项竞赛，7个领域，7,571张图，13类答案
build_method_en: Public competition PDFs and CS test cases, Mathpix conversion and annotation by about 30 STEM students, seven rule checks plus independent review, within-competition embedding deduplication, and human-verified GPT-4V labels
eval_feature_en: Bilingual, multidisciplinary, answer- and process-level evaluation, cognitive and visual reasoning labels
intro_en: OlympicArena is a bilingual multimodal Olympiad benchmark across seven scientific fields and 62 competitions. The paper defines 11,163 problems plus answer- and process-level protocols; the fixed Hugging Face snapshot publishes only 638 validation and 9,977 test problems, while the 548-problem OlympicArena-ot split is absent from that snapshot.
scale_en: Paper: 11,163 problems (548 OT + 638 validation + 9,977 test); fixed HF snapshot: 10,615, excluding the 548 OT problems; 62 competitions, 7 fields, 7,571 images, 13 answer types
metric_en: Paper: Accuracy, unbiased CS pass@1 with n=5, and mean process-step score; public code: keeps the full unboxed response, uses the extracted CS snippet count as effective n, and reports validation-set statistics

drawio_review_note: reviewed_at=2026-07-18. Primary-source audit fixed the paper to arXiv:2406.12753v2, last revised 2025-03-06; the downloaded PDF SHA-256 is bc6064edc79eb5ff826973fc4e9740570ce6c61155b86fdaf871fe6ca44f2ff9. The official GAIR-NLP/OlympicArena repository was inspected at immutable commit 99f6fa745ff8429f2951fd56a0d0ec580a9e00e2, and the public GAIR/OlympicArena Hugging Face dataset was inspected at immutable commit 001189f4e78bbdbe436770a2763a4283c6224709. Repository evidence includes README.md SHA-256 d1007bf0711aa126e584720bec1f2a3ae5d703848a0ccbeea1ceb49cfcaa9710, code/inference.py SHA-256 d2c60281bc466cefe80e70b9083413e0752ef31c5adecf7a838c643b93d0be1e, code/evaluation.py SHA-256 3d566f0dbae408cb6a19e488e116b081644e33824c5ee289ba12f3ced3b6b96e, code/judge.py SHA-256 7b673e1a7947ed6d5ea71d7ea252d001044b556559cce7064f1a4b1edea22874, and fixed HF README SHA-256 46577a40e26aaf072e9864ba2cdd000d1e713113816829aa27932b6c8141c9e6. The fixed HF card Paper field points to 2406.16772; this is incorrect for OlympicArena, whose paper and citation are 2406.12753, so the card field is retained only as source drift. Paper sections 3.1–3.4 and Appendix B establish the construction flow: collect URLs for publicly downloadable competition PDFs across mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology, geography, astronomy, and computer science; preserve available solutions and additionally collect CS test cases; obey copyright and licensing requirements; convert PDFs to Markdown with Mathpix; have about 30 science-and-engineering university students extract individual problems through the released Streamlit interface; store image URLs and one JSON object per problem; and retain solution metadata when provided. Appendix B.1 specifies seven interface checks rather than an unspecified generic validation step: numerical-value answers must not contain variables; non-numerical types must not parse as numerical values; expression answers must not contain an equals sign; equation answers must contain one; answers must not contain images; units belong in their separate field; and image links must preview. The two subsequent quality stages are a predefined-rule pass with correction and a second review by different annotators. Deduplication is within each competition and uses model embeddings to remove repeated problems appearing across test papers from the same year; the diagram does not claim global cross-competition deduplication. GPT-4V labels three difficulty levels only for the validation sets, per the paper footnote, and labels eight logical plus five visual abilities; all GPT-4V annotations are manually verified. The paper release totals are preserved exactly: 11,163 problems from 62 competitions and seven disciplines, 7,054 English plus 4,109 Chinese problems, 7,571 images, 4,960 image-bearing problems, 7,904 problems with solutions, and 13 answer types. Split arithmetic is explicit: 548 OlympicArena-ot problems designated for model-based evaluation, 638 OlympicArena-val problems with step-by-step solutions, and the remaining 9,977 OlympicArena-test problems with unreleased answers. The paper evaluates the entire benchmark, not merely the public validation payload, under multimodal, InternVL-Chat-V1.5 image-caption, and text-only zero-shot settings. Prompts are answer-type-specific, request LaTeX and a final boxed answer, use a 2,048-token maximum, temperature 0.0 generally, and 0.2 for code. Fixed answers go through boxed-answer extraction and type-specific rules covering numerical tolerance, symbolic equivalence with SymPy, intervals, sets, tuples, multiple quantities, and multiple answers. The paper requests a final boxed answer, but the fixed released parser has a boundary: Judger.extract_boxed_answer returns the full response when no well-formed non-empty box is found, and auto_judge continues on that text. The paper configuration generates five CS solutions, runs all test cases, and applies the unbiased pass@k expression with n=5 and k=1. The fixed inference implementation drops a generation when extract_code fails; evaluation.py then sets num_samples from the surviving code snippets, so effective n equals the extracted snippet count and may be below 5. The paper table and fixed public implementation have an aggregate boundary: evaluation.py retains the fractional pass@1 value for CS subject statistics, while its overall counter treats any nonzero pass@1 as one correct item; the diagram states this rather than flattening the two. Other-answer problems use GPT-4V with the problem, reference answer, optional solution, and tested response; a uniform sample of 100 produces nearly 80% human/model agreement, and this answer type is about 5% of the benchmark. Process-level evaluation is a separate 96-problem branch: GPT-4 first reformats gold and model solutions into steps, GPT-4V scores each step 0 or 1, each problem receives the mean step score, and sampled human checking reports 83% agreement. Publication was audited separately from the paper. The paper total of 11,163 equals 548 OT + 638 validation + 9,977 test, whereas HF commit 001189f4e78bbdbe436770a2763a4283c6224709 exposes seven subject configurations containing exactly 638 validation and 9,977 test rows, 10,615 total; OlympicArena-ot is not present in that fixed HF snapshot. Test answers are withheld. The pinned repository README and evaluation entrypoint support local scoring only on val and route test predictions to the submission platform, so the paper's entire benchmark experiment, public code validation evaluation, and server-side test submission are not interchangeable. The HF card marks the dataset CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. No construction steps, task counts, scorer semantics, or openness claims were inferred beyond these fixed paper, Git, and HF sources. Formal publication evidence [site-a12a-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 2773×861 (English) and 2773×861 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 2771×859 and 2771×859. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
